core_obligations: From a point of the site to a morphism of topoi (proof lines 8276-8281): the pair of functors is adjoint and the pullback is exact by definition of a point, so the conditions for a morphism of topoi hold.

From a point of the topos to the conditions of a point of the site (proof lines 8284-8299): the exactness of the pullback turns a surjection of representable sheaves into surjectivity of the corresponding map of sets, and the exactness of sheafification together with that of the pullback gives the compatibility with fibre products.

The comparison map (proof lines 8300-8325): the author constructs a canonical map from the stalk functor defined by the functor to the pullback of the point, shows that the two agree on representable sheaves using the companion results, and concludes for all sheaves because both functors commute with colimits and every sheaf is a coequalizer of coproducts of representables.
proof_roadmap: Turn a point of the site into a morphism of topoi using the exactness condition.
Verify the two conditions of a point of a site from exactness of the pullback and of sheafification.
Compare the resulting stalk functor with the pullback, first on representables and then through the coequalizer presentation.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the equivalence between points of a site and points of its topos: a point of the site gives a morphism of topoi from the topos of a point, and conversely a point of the topos gives a functor satisfying the conditions of a point of the site and a comparison isomorphism between the corresponding stalk functors (statement lines 8258-8273). The proof is a complete argument: one direction only checks the conditions of a morphism of topoi (proof lines 8276-8281); the other verifies the two conditions of a point of a site using exactness of the pullback and of sheafification (proof lines 8284-8299); and the comparison map is constructed, checked on representable sheaves and extended to all sheaves through the coequalizer presentation and the commutation of both functors with colimits (proof lines 8300-8325). The non-formal content is the comparison map and its verification on generators. The claim is H2: a structured argument carried out in three stages.
